notes: Only the advertised MCP tool `fetch` is judged. The source also defines a prompt named `fetch`, but it is not in the advertised tools list.
`max_length`, `start_index`, and `raw` affect formatting/truncation of returned content, not destination selection or stored/sent content.

fetch.rationale: `fetch` validates the caller-supplied `url` from the `Fetch` input schema and then uses it in `client.get(url, follow_redirects=True, headers={...})`, returning the fetched response text (or markdown extracted from it) in `TextContent.text`. Because the URL is agent-chosen and `AnyUrl` does not restrict to public internet hosts in the shown code, the tool can fetch `file://`, localhost, intranet, or other non-public reachable URLs if the HTTP client/URL handling permits them; under the rule, because this is not settled by the code, `SECRET` is kept and `undetermined` is true. It returns arbitrary web content controlled by attackers, so it is `UNTRUSTED`. It is also a `SINK` because a READ call to an agent-chosen URL/host sends an outbound request to that destination, and the threat model allows the agent to pass outputs into the `url`, path, or query. The same call may first request the origin's `/robots.txt` via `check_may_autonomously_fetch_url`, also derived from the supplied `url`. No arbitrary host code execution is shown.

value_conditions.effect: Default is false because `argparse` uses `action="store_true"`; when omitted, `call_tool` checks robots.txt before fetching. When supplied, the robots.txt check is skipped, but the `fetch` tool remains advertised and still performs the requested URL fetch, so labels are not removed.
Default is `None`; when supplied, both robots.txt and page fetches use `AsyncClient(proxy=proxy_url)`, changing network routing but not removing the tool or labels.
Default is the built-in autonomous/manual user agent strings; when supplied, requests use the custom User-Agent header, but the tool and labels remain.
